stem_book: Two identical rings, each of mass m and radius R, with their planes mutually perpendicular, are welded at their point of contact O (see figure: one ring is hung above the other; P is the topmost point of the upper ring, where it is pivoted, diametrically opposite O). If the system is free to rotate about an axis passing through the point P perpendicular to the plane of the paper, the moment of inertia of the system about this axis is equal to (a) 6.5 mR² (b) 12 mR² (c) 6 mR² (d) 11.5 mR²
reason: Manifest's bracketed description put O at the lower ring's centre, contradicting the print (O = weld point); stem rewritten from the print. Answer is the same whichever ring lies in the paper plane.
work: Upper ring in paper plane: 2mR²; lower ring ⊥ paper, centre 3R from P: mR²/2 + 9mR² ⇒ total 11.5 mR² (other orientation: 1.5mR² + 10mR² = 11.5 mR²)
